'''Richard B. Primack''' is an American plant ecologist and conservation biologist whose research focuses on the effects of climate change on plants and animals of [[New England]]. Widely regarded as the father of modern conservation biology, he has worked as a professor of biology at [[Boston University]] since 1978.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Academy of Europe: Primack Richard |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Primack_Richard |access-date=2025-08-13 |website=[[Academia Europaea]]}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Richard B. Primack |url=https://www.bu.edu/biology/people/profiles/richard-b-primack/ |access-date=2025-08-12 |website=[[Boston University|Boston University Department of Biology]]}}</ref>

Primack's book, ''Walden Warming'', and much of his research draws on records kept by [[Henry David Thoreau]] and other 19th-century naturalists in [[Concord, Massachusetts]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Alun |date=2014-04-09 |title=What climate change has done to Walden's woods |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg22229640-900-what-climate-change-has-done-to-waldens-woods/ |access-date=2025-08-13 |website=[[New Scientist]] |language=en-US}}</ref> His lab group pioneered the use of non-traditional data sources to investigate the effects of climate change, including photographs, museum specimens, citizen science networks, naturalist diaries, and experiments using dormant twigs.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sparks |first=Tim H. |date=2007-04-01 |title=Lateral thinking on data to identify climate impacts |url=https://www.cell.com/trends/ecology-evolution/abstract/S0169-5347(07)00023-7 |journal=Trends in Ecology & Evolution |language=English |volume=22 |issue=4 |pages=169–171 |doi=10.1016/j.tree.2007.01.003 |issn=0169-5347 |pmid=17267072 |bibcode=2007TEcoE..22..169S |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2008-10-27 |title=Thoreau Is Rediscovered as a Climatologist (Published 2008) |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/10/28/science/earth/28wald.html |access-date=2025-10-21 |work=The New York Times |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-02-06 |title=Citizen Science Takes Root |url=https://www.americanscientist.org/article/citizen-science-takes-root |access-date=2025-10-21 |website=American Scientist |language=en}}</ref> He served as == Early life and education ==
Primack grew up in [[Newton, Massachusetts]] and attended Newton South High School. He attended [[Harvard College]], where he majored in biology. As a result of a course at the [[Harvard Forest]], he decided to switch his career path from medicine to botany. For his undergraduate thesis, he surveyed the flora of the Hammond Woods and Webster Woods in Newton.

Primack attended graduate school at [[Duke University]], where he completed his PhD in plant [[population biology]] with Janis Antonovics. Primack then carried out two post-doctoral research projects: the first studying mountain shrub ecology with David Lloyd at the [[University of Canterbury]] in [[New Zealand]], and the second studying [[tropical ecology]] of forests in [[Sarawak|Sarawak, Malaysia]] with [[Peter Shaw Ashton]] at Harvard University. 

== Research ==
Primack has authored or coauthored more than 210 peer-reviewed scientific papers and his writings have been cited more than 25,000 times. His most highly cited publications are his conservation biology textbooks, papers on the ecological effects of climate change on [[phenology]], and papers on flower longevity and pollination ecology.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Richard Primack |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=XfgB_BUAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=ao |access-date=2025-10-23 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>

=== Impacts of climate change in eastern Massachusetts ===
Primack's most recent research focuses on the impacts of climate change on the flowering, fruiting, leaf out, and leaf senescence times of plants, the spring arrival and autumn departure of birds, and the timing and diversity of insects visiting flowers in Massachusetts. This research has focused on eastern Massachusetts because of the availability of historical natural history records in the region. These records include extensive records of flowering, leaf out, bird arrivals, and other phenological events made by Henry David Thoreau in the 1850s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Primack |first1=Richard B. |last2=Miller-Rushing |first2=Abraham J. |date=2024 |title=Thoreau's Contributions to Climate Change Science |url=https://muse.jhu.edu/pub/562/article/942977 |journal=The Dial: A Journal of the Ralph Waldo Emerson Society |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=76–96 |doi=10.1353/dial.2024.a942977 |issn=3065-5447|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

=== The role of botanical gardens in climate change research ===
Much of Primack's research has been carried out at botanical gardens, especially the [[Arnold Arboretum]] of Harvard University. He has written about the  importance of botanical gardens in climate change research and has facilitated the creation of international networks of botanical gardens to investigate questions about how plants are responding to climate change.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Primack |first1=Richard B. |last2=Ellwood |first2=Elizabeth R. |last3=Gallinat |first3=Amanda S. |last4=Miller-Rushing |first4=Abraham J. |date=2021 |title=The growing and vital role of botanical gardens in climate change research |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/nph.17410 |journal=New Phytologist |language=en |volume=231 |issue=3 |pages=917–932 |doi=10.1111/nph.17410 |pmid=33890323 |bibcode=2021NewPh.231..917P |issn=1469-8137|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Panchen |first1=Zoe A. |last2=Primack |first2=Richard B. |last3=Gallinat |first3=Amanda S. |last4=Nordt |first4=Birgit |last5=Stevens |first5=Albert-Dieter |last6=Du |first6=Yanjun |last7=Fahey |first7=Robert |date=2015 |title=Substantial variation in leaf senescence times among 1360 temperate woody plant species: implications for phenology and ecosystem processes |journal=Annals of Botany |language=en |volume=116 |issue=6 |pages=865–873 |doi=10.1093/aob/mcv015 |issn=1095-8290 |pmc=4640117 |pmid=25808654}}</ref>

=== Tropical forest biology ===
Primack has investigated how [[Rainforest|rain forests]] in [[East Malaysia|Malaysian Borneo]] change over time in terms of species diversity and forest structure, and how selective logging affects these processes. Primack worked with Richard Corlett to write a book, ''Tropical Rain Forests: An Ecological and Biogeographical Comparison'', contrasting tropical rain forests on different continents.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Corlett |first1=Richard |title=Tropical rain forests: an ecological and biogeographical comparison |last2=Primack |first2=Richard B. |date=2011 |publisher=Wiley-Blackwell |isbn=978-1-4443-3254-4 |edition=2nd |location=Chichester, West Sussex Hoboken, NJ}}</ref> 

=== Impacts of COVID-19 pandemic on conservation ===
Primack has worked with colleagues to describe the impacts of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and the associated lockdowns and changes in human activity on conservation. These projects have examined impacts on US national parks, noise pollution, and the formation of social trails in protected areas.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Primack |first1=Richard B. |last2=Bates |first2=Amanda E. |last3=Duarte |first3=Carlos M. |date=2021-08-01 |title=The conservation and ecological impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic |journal=Biological Conservation |volume=260 |article-number=109204 |doi=10.1016/j.biocon.2021.109204 |issn=0006-3207 |pmc=9746885 |pmid=36533167 |bibcode=2021BCons.26009204P |hdl=10754/669734 }}</ref>

=== Leading the scientific journal ''Biological Conservation'' ===
As editor-in-chief of ''Biological Conservation'', Primack handled approximately 17,000 manuscripts, of which 3,000 were published following peer-review. During his tenure, the journal published special issues on a range of topics, including several that highlighted research of scientists from under-represented countries. Primack authored editorials and papers about the publication process and the careers of scientists, including pieces about the challenges faced by women ecologists and scientists from developing countries.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Devictor |first1=Vincent |last2=Descoteaux |first2=Danielle |date=2021-01-01 |title=Hats off and warm thanks to Richard Primack |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0006320720309307 |journal=Biological Conservation |volume=253 |article-number=108872 |doi=10.1016/j.biocon.2020.108872 |bibcode=2021BCons.25308872D |issn=0006-3207|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Conservation biology textbook project ==
Primack authored two of the first textbooks in the field of conservation biology: ''Essentials of Conservation Biology'' and ''A Primer of Conservation Biology'', both of which were published in multiple editions starting in 1993.<ref>{{Citation |last=Sarkar |first=Sahotra |title=Conservation Biology |date=2004 |encyclopedia=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy |editor-last=Zalta |editor-first=Edward N. |url=https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/sum2004/entries/conservation-biology/ |access-date=2025-10-22 |edition=Summer 2004 |publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University |editor2-last=Nodelman |editor2-first=Uri}}</ref> More recently, he worked with coauthors to write newer textbooks: ''An Introduction to Conservation Biology'', written with [[Anna Sher]], and ''Conservation Biology'', and advanced textbook written with [[Bradley Cardinale]] and Jed Murdoch. 

Primack worked with co-authors in foreign countries to produce 38 foreign-language and international editions of these textbooks with local conservation examples. The intent was to support training in conservation biology and the protection of biodiversity worldwide.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Boston professor adapting biology textbook for other countries - The Boston Globe |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2013/12/23/boston-professor-adapting-biology-textbook-for-other-countries/hQ6gz3I8Hw30j9yPqTNBeO/story.html |access-date=2025-10-23 |website=BostonGlobe.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |date=2013 |title=Locally Adapted Textbooks Can Help Biodiversity |url=https://academic.oup.com/bioscience/article-lookup/doi/10.1525/bio.2013.63.12.5 |journal=BioScience |language=en |volume=63 |issue=12 |pages=926–927 |doi=10.1525/bio.2013.63.12.5|url-access=subscription }}</ref> The most recent book from this project is a free online textbook, ''Conservation Biology in Sub-Saharan Africa'', which has been downloaded more than 50,000 times.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Wilson |first1=John W. |title=Conservation Biology in Sub-Saharan Africa |last2=Primack |first2=Richard B. |date=2019-09-08 |publisher=Open Book Publishers |isbn=978-1-78374-750-4 |language=English |doi=10.11647/obp.0177 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Teaching and outreach ==
At Boston University, Primack teaches courses in conservation biology and plant biology. Primack has appeared on major media outlets, including ''The New York Times'', ''Boston Globe'', and NPR, to discuss his research and to comment on stories related to on climate change, conservation, and ecology.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2014-04-23 |title=Springing Forward, and Its Consequences (Published 2014) |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/04/24/science/springing-forward-and-its-consequences.html |access-date=2025-10-22 |work=The New York Times |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Can Thoreau make us care about forest wildflowers? - The Boston Globe |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/globelocal/2019/03/01/can-thoreau-make-care-about-forest-wildflowers/ZDloq3imqIw0boCxC69rwM/story.html |access-date=2025-10-22 |website=BostonGlobe.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-22 |title=Flowers and trees are blooming earlier. Is it because of climate change? : Short Wave |url=https://www.npr.org/2025/04/22/1266983681/spring-flowers-earth-day-phenology |access-date=2025-10-22 |website=NPR |language=en}}</ref> He often gives talks to the public and writes for popular outlets. Primack has also collaborated with museums on exhibits featuring his research.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Early Spring: Henry Thoreau and Climate Change |url=https://concordmuseum.org/online-exhibition/early-spring-henry-thoreau-and-climate-change/ |access-date=2025-10-22 |website=Concord Museum |language=en-US}}</ref> And he is involved in local conservation in his hometown of Newton, Massachusetts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Scott |date=2016-06-22 |title=The Science of Webster Woods |url=https://newtonconservators.org/the-science-of-webster-woods/ |access-date=2025-10-22 |website=Newton Conservators |language=en-US}}</ref>
